label: Editorial
summary: The page reads like a well art directed feature: type carries the hierarchy, photographs are placed like spreads, and whitespace is a material, not leftover space.

heroes.notes: A headline block set large in the display face, aligned to a column grid, with one photograph given real size. Never a centred stack over a stock background.

navigation.notes: Few links set small, often uppercase with open tracking; the wordmark behaves like a masthead.

typography.notes: A display face with real contrast or character at 56 to 96px on desktop, a restrained body at 17 to 19px with a 60 to 72 character measure, small caps or tracked labels for section eyebrows.

layout.notes: Section widths vary on purpose (a narrow text column, then a full width image, then an offset pair). Numbered sections and hairline rules give structure instead of boxes.

geometry.notes: Corners stay square or nearly square; 1px rules and alignment do the work cards would do elsewhere.

imagery.notes: Fewer, larger photographs with captions set like figure notes. Consistent crops and colour grading; detail shots next to wide shots.

motion.notes: Quiet: fades and short rises on first reveal, underline and colour changes on hover. Nothing bounces, nothing loops behind the text.

principles: Let typography create the hierarchy: one display size per screen, generous leading, a real measure for reading text.
Give photographs editorial weight: few, large, captioned, cropped with intent, never a grid of small equal thumbnails as the main proof.
Structure with rules, numbers and alignment instead of boxes and shadows; a section is a spread, not a card.
Vary section width and rhythm deliberately so the page reads as a sequence, not a stack of identical bands.
Keep the conversion obvious but calm: one understated primary action per screen in the display or body face, never a loud badge.
Captions and labels carry facts plainly; flourish belongs to the type, never to claims.
